title: EDA
text:
The Water Potability dataset contains measurements of water quality, including variables such as pH, hardness, solids, chloramines, sulfate, conductivity, and turbidity. The response variable is Potability, which indicates whether the water is safe to drink.
The purpose of this exploratory data analysis is to better understand the data, check for any data quality issues, and explore relationships between the predictors and water potability. These results will help prepare the data for predictive modeling.

title: EDA
text:
Graphical Summaries

Distribution of Potability

ggplot(water, aes(Potability)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Water Potability",
    x = "Potability",
    y = "Count"
  )








This plot shows the number of potable and non-potable water samples.


Distribution of pH

ggplot(water, aes(ph)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of pH",
    x = "pH",
    y = "Count"
  )

Warning: Removed 491 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
(`stat_bin()`).









Most water samples have pH values near the middle of the observed range.


pH by Potability

ggplot(water, aes(Potability, ph, fill = Potability)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "pH by Water Potability",
    x = "Potability",
    y = "pH"
  )

Warning: Removed 491 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
(`stat_boxplot()`).









This plot compares the distribution of pH values for potable and non-potable water.
